name: Merger arbitrage
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Earning the Deal Completion Spread
caseLead: Merger arbitrage seeks to earn the difference between a takeover target's share price and the agreed offer price, which compensates for the possibility that the deal fails. The spread can persist because some investors sell after an announcement, while merger funds must bear completion delays, regulatory reviews and the possibility of a deal being blocked.
caseRest: The main risk is deal failure, which can drive the target's share price back towards its level before the announcement. Losses cluster when many deals come under stress together, as in a market sell-off that widens spreads on every pending deal. The estimated 7.4% annual return therefore comes with 4.2% volatility, a 10.0% worst fall and strongly negative return skew, so a long run of completed deals understates the loss from a single failure.
figNote: Each card shows the announced value of the deal in billions of US dollars. Larger deals attract more regulatory and political scrutiny, which is the main reason a deal that investors expect to complete can be delayed or blocked.

events.title: Lehman failure widens spreads on pending deals
events.text: Lehman Brothers' failure in September 2008 froze acquisition financing and widened spreads on pending deals, including InBev's $52bn offer for Anheuser-Busch. Results were mixed because that deal closed in November, while several leveraged buyouts were abandoned.

events.title: US tax rules end Pfizer and Allergan deal
events.text: New US Treasury rules against tax inversions in April 2016 led Pfizer to terminate its $160bn merger with Allergan. The strategy lost because Allergan's share price fell sharply once the premium to the offer price disappeared.

events.title: Missing Chinese approval ends Qualcomm and NXP deal
events.text: Qualcomm abandoned its $44bn purchase of NXP Semiconductors in July 2018 because Chinese regulators had not approved it during the US-China trade dispute. The strategy lost because NXP's share price fell back towards its undisturbed level.

events.title: Disney completes Fox purchase after approvals
events.text: Disney completed its $71bn purchase of 21st Century Fox in March 2019 after US and international regulators approved the deal. The strategy gained because the target's shares converged to the offer value, so the full spread was earned.

events.title: Microsoft completes Activision purchase after long review
events.text: Microsoft completed its $69bn purchase of Activision Blizzard in October 2023 after a US court rejected a challenge and UK regulators accepted revised terms. The strategy gained because the wide spread was earned in full, although capital was tied up for almost two years.

events.title: Nippon Steel completes US Steel purchase after reversal
events.text: Nippon Steel completed its $15bn purchase of US Steel in June 2025 after President Trump approved it with national security conditions, five months after President Biden blocked it. Results were mixed because the spread widened after the block and then closed on approval.

instrument: Listed shares of announced takeover targets; held until completion, typically three to six months
rules: Targets bought after a definitive offer when the spread exceeds the cash rate plus estimated failure risk; acquirer shares sold short in stock deals; deals needing several regulatory approvals sized smaller
costs: Estimated bid-ask spreads, commissions and share borrowing costs deducted
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from deal spread to failure protection

legs.purpose: Earns the spread to the offer price
Earns the spread after hedging acquirer risk
Limits losses when many deals are stressed at once
Provides collateral and earns the cash rate

entry: Annualised spread at least 4 points above the cash rate
size: Single deal capped at 5%; set to a 4% annualised volatility target
exit: Position closed when the deal completes, or when the spread falls below 0.5%
stop: Position closed if the target falls 8% below the offer price
marketWatch: Spreads on pending deals relative to the cash rate and the pace of regulatory reviews are the main indicators because they show how much compensation investors receive for completion risk. Antitrust enforcement, national security reviews and approval timetables in China matter most when they extend the time to completion or raise the chance of a block.

favourable.heading: Regulators approve deals promptly
favourable.text: Prompt regulatory approval favours the strategy because the spread is earned over a shorter period, which raises the annualised return. In 2019, Disney's Fox purchase and other large deals closed after clear regulatory timetables.

favourable.heading: Credit markets stay open
favourable.text: Open financing markets favour the strategy because buyers can fund cash offers and lenders remain willing to support leveraged deals. Strong bond issuance in 2013 and 2014 helped most announced deals to close on schedule.

favourable.heading: Rival bidders emerge
favourable.text: A rival bid favours the strategy because the target's share price rises above the original offer, so holders earn more than the spread. In 2018, Comcast's challenge to Disney's offer for Fox led Disney to raise its price.

adverse.heading: Governments block deals
adverse.text: Blocked deals hurt the strategy because the target price falls to its pre-deal level, erasing months of spread income in one day. In 2016, new US tax rules ended Pfizer's $160bn offer for Allergan, and in 2018 Chinese approval did not arrive for Qualcomm's purchase of NXP.

adverse.heading: Market sell-offs widen spreads
adverse.text: A broad sell-off hurts the strategy because investors demand more compensation for deal risk, so spreads widen on every pending deal at once. In March 2020, spreads on announced deals widened sharply as funds sold positions to raise cash.

adverse.heading: Buyers lose their financing
adverse.text: Withdrawn financing hurts the strategy because buyers can renegotiate or abandon deals when lenders stop supporting them. In 2008 and 2009, several leveraged buyouts were abandoned, including the Hexion offer for Huntsman.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's estimated peak-to-trough change in value during each event, using the spreads on the deals then pending and the outcome of each deal. Each event window runs from the last market high before the shock to the market low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in equity prices, credit spreads and regulatory approval odds, which are then applied to the strategy's pending deals, including those that need Chinese approval.
